title: Down-home music and blues as secular spirituals
summary: He explains 'down home' meant blues, Blue Monday and homesickness, and that blues grew out of ring shouts as secular music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Was a term used like 'down home'? You talk about some music being 'down home'.
Yes. Well, when they had reference to the down home, well they had reference to the blues, then.

See? That was blues music, and a lot of people -- and how the blues really got started was in -- for down home was people, fellas that had left home and was trying to make it and they couldn't make it so they returned home, you know? And you usually hear the railroad whistle blowing, toot-toot, and they was thinking about the time they used to sit under the honeysuckle vine and --

And spoon out by a harvest moon, and all that, like down home. So they got so when they were away from home, it was like blue monday. Blue Monday started, like these guys were away from home, and they were thinking, 'Oh, oh.' And so they were writing music like it's going to take me back home. A lot of them, see, them standing on the railroad track, waiting for my honey to come back. It'll be the last time I wait around for you.
Well, all those things had a meaning, you know?

And the blues. But now, I wanted to say one thing here. Blues was not a new music. Blues come off the ring shout and what you would call the approach to the spiritual. The, the, the word has slipped my mind now. You know, the approach to a spiritual that is not sacred.
So, but the blues were, it's a part of the negroe --

That's the word I wanted. Yeah. It was secular, the same as the Bach Chorale had a seculars form, too. You know, there was many chorales, even written during Bach's time, on the secular music. They turned around and made it religious. But really, the beginning of it was from the minne-singers and the heralds and the people, the jongleurs, that travelled around singing. So, and the same way with the black music.
